stem: How is hypospadias classified when the urethral opening is located between the coronal sulcus and the midshaft of the penis?
explanation: This classification is used when the urethral meatus is positioned between the coronal sulcus and the middle of the shaft.
rationale: This term describes the central region of the penile shaft.

optionExplanations.A: Distal (or anterior) hypospadias occurs when the opening is at the coronal sulcus or further toward the tip.
optionExplanations.B: This classification is used when the urethral meatus is positioned between the coronal sulcus and the middle of the shaft.
optionExplanations.C: Proximal (or posterior) hypospadias refers to openings located closer to the base of the penis or the scrotum.
optionExplanations.D: 'Ectopic' is not a standard classification term for the position of the urethral opening in hypospadias.

source.hint: This term describes the central region of the penile shaft.
